nodes.name: Export All Rows (Notion)
nodes.notes: Pulls every page from the Notion database — fine for small datasets; add a filter if the database grows large. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Serialize to CSV
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Compress Archive
nodes.notes: Zips the binary to cut storage/transfer size before upload.

parameters.content:
# Back up the database with Slack

**Pattern:** Backup & Archive · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers webhooks work end to end across Slack, Notion, Google Drive and Microsoft Teams.

It moves through 12 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Export All Rows (Notion)
3. Serialize to CSV
4. Compress Archive
5. Upload Backup to Google Drive
6. Backup Size Sane?
7. Alarm — Empty Backup
8. Align Field Names
9. Tag Pipeline Metadata
10. Save Execution Metadata
11. Sort Payloads Newest First
12. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing webhooks work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Export All Rows (Notion) → Serialize to CSV → Compress Archive → Upload Backup to Google Drive → Backup Size Sane? → Alarm — Empty Backup → Align Field Names → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Save Execution Metadata → Sort Payloads Newest First → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Notion aligned by hand for webhooks
- Webhooks work where "Export All Rows (Notion)" is still a manual step before Slack
- Webhooks work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Notion in step for webhooks, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 14 nodes in this webhooks build
- Every webhooks run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack
- Fans the same result out to Google Drive in the same run, for webhooks
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 14 nodes for webhooks before wiring Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The empty-backup check exists because a backup that silently 'succeeds' with zero rows is worse than an obvious failure — it gives false confidence right up until the day you actually need to restore. Compression runs before upload, not after, cutting both transfer time and storage footprint in the same step.

## Practice exercises

Once it's wired up with real credentials, try:

1. Point the export at an empty table on purpose and confirm the alarm fires.
2. Turn off compression and compare the resulting backup file size.
3. Add a retention step that deletes backups older than N days from the destination.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your webhooks process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole webhooks payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
